summary.headline: Hero MotoCorp Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to INR14,687 crores, with EBITDA margin at 13.4% and VIDA turning gross-margin positive.
summary.overview: Wholesale volume grew 10.5% YoY, with ICE up 8.4% and EV up 98%, and revenue growth of 21% was helped by a 5% mix benefit and calibrated pricing. EBITDA rose 8% YoY to INR1,968 crores and PAT rose 5% YoY to INR1,456 crores on a standalone basis, while consolidated PAT grew 41% to INR1,861 crores including a INR397 crore one-time associate gain. Gross margin fell 30 bps QoQ, but overhead control lifted EBITDA margin 10 bps QoQ. Exports were hit by Colombia and Bangladesh disruptions, while domestic ICE share gains continued.

financial_highlights.value: INR1,861 crores; includes INR397 crore one-time associate gain

financial_highlights.change: nearly doubled vs prior comparable period

financial_highlights.value: Turned gross-margin positive; EV drag INR168 crores vs INR232 crores in Q1

segments.name: India ICE two-wheelers
segments.commentary: ICE retail grew 24% YoY in Q2 with market share gains in every month; ICE scooter dispatches up 34% YoY in Q2 and above 50% in H1. ICE segment EBITDA margin was 15.6% in the prior quarter, per management.

segments.name: EV (VIDA / EM BU)
segments.commentary: VIDA retail rose 74% YoY to 66,000 units in Q2; EV revenue about INR1,000 crores; production ramped to 30,000 units/month in September. Market share hit about 13.5-14% in October month-to-date.

segments.name: Parts, accessories and merchandise
segments.commentary: Revenue up 27% YoY, second straight quarter above 25%. Global Parts Center 2.0 greenfield investment of over INR700 crores to double parts handling capacity.

segments.name: Global business / exports
segments.commentary: Colombia (about 25% of exports) and Bangladesh were hit by an earthquake-linked port/clearance issue and a demand slowdown, lowering wholesale; retail still grew 19%. Management expects double-digit wholesale growth in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Premium
segments.commentary: Premium business unit carved out in Q2; Xtreme 160R and 250R launched in October; over 30% retail growth in H1 and over 35% share in adventure bikes. Premia network about 150 stores; 3-4 more premium launches planned in H2.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 EBITDA margin expected to remain stable despite a marginal uptick in input costs from West Asia conflict and commodity inflation.
Medium-term EBITDA margin target corridor of 14% to 16%; management expects to reach it in the next few quarters as commodities stabilise.
FY27 capex guidance of INR1,500 crores reaffirmed; about INR600 crores spent in H1.
Industry growth for H2 FY27 expected at mid-to-high single digits, with ICE at low single digits and EV taking it to high single digits.
VIDA capacity to rise from 30,000 to 45,000 units/month in Q4 FY27 and to over 80,000 units/month by Q2 FY28.
PLI benefit expected to cover about 13% of revenue from Q3, as certification covers nearly 100% of EV portfolio (about 70% previously).
capex_capacity: VIDA EV capacity raised to 30,000 units/month in September 2026 from 15,000 at end FY26; target 45,000 in Q4 and over 80,000 by Q2 FY28.
ICE scooter capacity doubled to about 80,000 units/month through Destini and Xoom expansions; further Xoom capacity planned.
Splendor capacity expanded; dedicated premium assembly line expanded at Neemrana.
Global Parts Center 2.0 Phase II at Tirupati to be fully operational by end of calendar 2027; over INR700 crores invested in automated parts centre.
Brazil manufacturing facility being set up for flex-fuel vehicles.
demand_pricing: Industry VAHAN retail grew over 27% in Q2 (ICE 23%, EV 82%); H1 retail over 20% YoY; two-year CAGR 11%.
Rural performance equal to or better than urban in Q2 and quarter-to-date, per management.
Festival-to-date (100-day festive period) growth of 24% with no share erosion; dealer stock about 1 day, described as capacity-constrained.
Revenue growth of 21% vs volume 10.5% reflects 5% positive mix impact plus calibrated pricing.
Material inflation about 5.5% over Q1 and Q2; about half recovered through price increases; price hike of about INR1,000 per unit taken on 1 October.
Splendor grew over 20%; XTEC above 25% of Splendor volumes; 100cc category up 10% in Q2 and 11% in H1; 125cc up 19% in H1 but category soft.

qa_highlights.question: How big are Colombia and Bangladesh in exports, and when can export distribution become more balanced?
qa_highlights.answer: Colombia is close to 25% of exports and Bangladesh is also large; both were hit in the same quarter. Recovery was seen by quarter-end. Brazil (with a planned plant and flex-fuel range), Mexico and Africa are the expansion focus.

qa_highlights.question: What are the EV drag, EV revenue and commodity inflation figures, and how does PLI scale?
qa_highlights.answer: EV drag was about INR168 crores in Q2 vs INR232 crores in Q1; EV revenue about INR1,000 crores; commodity inflation about 1% QoQ. PLI was INR63 crores (about 6.5% of revenue) covering 70% of the portfolio; management expects about 13% of revenue from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why were other expenses down, and when will margins return to 14-16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower other expenses reflect discretionary budget cuts taken in Q2 to offset material inflation. Management expects to reach the target range in the next few quarters, helped by premium mix, the Premia network, EV unit economics, LEAP savings and calibrated pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company prioritising market share or margin, given discretionary cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Harsh Chitale said growth and share are the priority and investment will not be cut. Margin recovery will come from unit economics, volume leverage and LEAP BOM savings. ICE share was gained in every month of Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin drag from EV and when does VIDA reach EBITDA break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the EV margin drag is about 220 bps at company level. VIDA is still a path ahead to EBITDA positive, as portfolio completion and scale are needed. Charging network of over 6,000 points is being monetised, and tie-ups with Euler and Ather are limited to go-to-market and charging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the premium bike launch plan and the flex-fuel uptake?
qa_highlights.answer: Four premium brands are drivers: Xtreme, Xpulse, Karizma and Harley-Davidson co-developed products, with launches across all four. Flex-fuel has about 15,000 dispatches in just over two months, in controlled launch at select dealerships.

risks_watch: Export concentration: Colombia (about 25% of exports) and Bangladesh disruptions; Q3 double-digit wholesale recovery needs to be verified.
Commodity inflation from West Asia conflict and currency depreciation; margins guided only as stable in Q3.
Margin recovery depends on LEAP savings, PLI ramp and price actions; discretionary spend cuts could affect brand investment.
EV capacity ramp to 45,000 units/month by Q4 and profitability, with VIDA still EBITDA negative.
125cc category softness versus share gains; premium segment traction still early.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, market share and EV ramp, but cautious on margins, which management says will hold stable in Q3 and return to the 14-16% corridor only over the next few quarters. Management was direct about export disruption and defensive when asked about discretionary cuts.
key_quotes: Clearly, we are focused on growth and market share expansion. So we are not going to compromise or cut down on investments needed for driving growth and market share expansion.
Backed by these measures, we expect margins in quarter 3 to remain stable.
we are working with a dealer stock of just about 1 day, which shows that actually, we are still capacity constrained

adds.what: VIDA EV capacity raised to 30,000 units/month (from 15,000 at end FY26)
VIDA EV capacity to over 80,000 units/month by Q2 FY28
ICE scooter capacity doubled to about 80,000 units/month via Destini and Xoom expansions
Global Parts Center 2.0 Phase II at Tirupati, parts handling capacity doubled, over INR700 crore invested

growth.why: Management guides double-digit wholesale growth in Q3 and Q4 and H2 industry growth of mid-to-high single digits, backed by VIDA capacity rising from 30,000 to 45,000/month in Q4 FY27 and over 80,000 by Q2 FY28, with ICE scooter capacity already doubled to about 80,000/month and a 1-day dealer stock signalling constraints.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q3 EBITDA margin guided stable despite input cost uptick; medium-term 14-16% corridor expected 'in the next few quarters' from current 13.4% margin, helped by PLI covering ~13% of revenue from Q3 (INR63 crore PLI ~6.5% of revenue in Q2) and EV drag falling to INR168 crore from INR232 crore.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: VIDA capacity already raised from 15,000 to 30,000 units/month in September 2026, with 45,000 under way for Q4 FY27 and over 80,000 by Q2 FY28; ICE scooter capacity already doubled to about 80,000/month.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides double-digit wholesale growth in Q3 and Q4 after Colombia/Bangladesh disruption; Q2 wholesale was +10.5% YoY with ICE retail +24% and VIDA retail +74% to 66,000 units, and dealer stock is about 1 day, described as capacity-constrained.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capacity is constrained (1-day dealer stock, festival growth 24%) and VIDA needs to go from 45,000 to 80,000+/month by Q2 FY28, with FY27 capex of INR1,500 crore reaffirmed and only about INR600 crore spent in H1; further Xoom capacity and Brazil flex-fuel plant are also in progress.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the capex and EV capacity guides, cut H2 industry growth to mid-to-high single digits, and guided Q3 margin only stable amid West Asia and commodity inflation of about 5.5% over Q1 and Q2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 margin only guided stable and H2 industry growth cut to mid-to-high single digits; Colombia (about 25% of exports) and Bangladesh disruption and West Asia commodity risks could derail the double-digit wholesale recovery.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans 3-4 more premium launches in H2 on top of Xtreme 160R and 250R launched in October, and flex-fuel already has about 15,000 dispatches in controlled launch.

rows.label: Brazil flex-fuel manufacturing facility
rows.why: Brazil manufacturing facility is being set up for flex-fuel vehicles, with Brazil, Mexico and Africa named as export expansion focus, but no date or size was given.

rows.label: PLI benefit ramp to ~13% of revenue
rows.why: PLI certification covers nearly 100% of EV portfolio (about 70% before), lifting PLI from INR63 crore (about 6.5% of revenue) toward about 13% of revenue from Q3.

rows.label: Price hike of about INR1,000 per unit
rows.why: Price increase taken on 1 October against material inflation of about 5.5% over Q1 and Q2, with about half recovered through price increases so far.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, share gains and the VIDA ramp, but cautious on Q3 margins and defensive on discretionary spend cuts; analysts pressed on margin recovery, the discretionary cuts and export disruption.
